base_prompt: Why can a metal spoon feel colder than a wooden spoon even when both have been sitting in the same room all night? Explain for a curious teenager. Keep your response near 80 words.
text: Both spoons are probably at the same room temperature, but metal feels colder because it conducts heat much better than wood. When you touch the metal spoon, heat quickly flows from your warmer hand into the spoon, cooling your skin and creating a strong “cold” sensation. Wood transfers heat much more slowly, so your skin stays warmer and the spoon feels less cold. Your nerves sense the rate of heat loss, not just an object’s actual temperature.
